authorization: User explicitly supplied hypothetical cost points, a 1.2 LRT/BRT ridership ratio and 15-signal travel-time assumptions in this conversation.
cost_basis: Common hypothetical CAD scenario units by user assumption, not an inflation-adjusted transfer of historical project costs. Complete scope/price-year reconciliation remains open.
ridership_basis: Relative index with BRT=1; no absolute daily or peak-hour prediction is fabricated.
time_basis: User-assumed minutes saved per one-way end-to-end trip on a common hypothetical baseline; not measured Finch East savings or average passenger savings.
point_estimate_basis: User-selected rounded points, not exact interval midpoints. Previous BRT [0.29,0.40]B midpoint=0.345B; LRT [0.77,1.20]B midpoint=0.985B.
engineering_claim: Surface BRT and LRT are conditional options. LRT is not assumed fully grade-separated; larger vehicle capacity does not by itself prove higher ridership or superior TSP response.
weight_basis: Analyst-declared preferences for sensitivity analysis; no stakeholder elicitation or empirical weight estimate. Efficiency includes ridership, so explicit ridership also creates conceptual overlap; inverse-cost sensitivity removes that overlap.
weight_prior: Dirichlet(1,1,1), illustrative uniform criterion-weight simplex; fixed baseline input assumptions, no cost/demand/time sampling and no statistical confidence claim.
stress_basis: Deterministic analyst stress assumptions, not confidence intervals, full capital estimates or probabilities of project outcomes.
